name: Battle of Ain Jalut

sides.name: Mongols of the Ilkhanate and their vassals

phases.title: The Mongols hold the spring
phases.text: Kitbuqa reached Ain Jalut first and camped by the spring, with Mount Gilboa covering one flank. Baibars, leading the Mamluk vanguard, sighted the camp from a height, while Qutuz hid the bulk of his army in the highlands.

phases.title: The Mongols advance and Baibars strikes and runs
phases.text: The Mongols moved first. For many hours Baibars provoked them with hit-and-run attacks and kept most of his men out of the fight.

phases.title: Baibars feigns a final retreat
phases.text: After another heavy Mongol assault Baibars and his men pretended to break and rode back towards the highlands. The aim was to draw the Mongols after them into an ambush.

phases.title: Kitbuqa follows with all his troops
phases.text: Kitbuqa, already provoked by the constant flight of Baibars and his men, did not suspect a trick. He marched forward with all of his troops on the trail of the fleeing Mamluks.

phases.title: The trap closes
phases.text: When the Mongols reached the highlands the hidden Mamluks came out, shooting arrows and charging with their cavalry. The Mongols found themselves surrounded.

phases.title: The Mongols fight to break out
phases.text: The Mongol army fought aggressively to break out of the ring. Their attack almost destroyed the Mamluk left wing, which gave way before it.

phases.title: Qutuz throws away his helmet and charges
phases.text: Qutuz saw the left wing almost destroyed. He threw away his combat helmet so that his warriors could recognise him, then rushed towards the weakened side, followed by his own unit.

phases.title: The Mongols are pushed back towards Baysan
phases.text: The Mongols were pushed back by the Mamluk attack and fled to the neighbourhood of Baysan. Qutuz’s forces followed them eastwards across the field.

phases.title: The Mongols reorganise and counter-attack
phases.text: The Mongols managed to reorganise and returned to the battlefield, where they made a successful counter-attack.

phases.title: The battle turns and Kitbuqa dies
phases.text: The battle then shifted towards the Mamluks, who held the advantage of ground and morale. Some of the Mongols were forced to retreat, and Kitbuqa perished with almost all the rest of the army that remained in the region.

note: The highlands where the Mamluks hid are placed on their side of the field; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay.
